title: Thermodynamics
syllabus: Thermal equilibrium, Zeroth law of thermodynamics, Concept of temperature, Heat, Work and internal energy, First law of thermodynamics, Isothermal and adiabatic processes, Isobaric and isochoric processes, Cyclic and non-cyclic processes, Second law of thermodynamics, Reversible and irreversible processes, Heat engines and refrigerators

questions.question: In an adiabatic process, the pressure is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature. The ratio $\gamma = C_p / C_v$ for the gas is: (NEET 2023)
questions.solution:
In an adiabatic process: $P^{1-\gamma} T^\gamma = \text{constant} \implies P \propto T^{\frac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1}}$.
Given $P \propto T^3 \implies \frac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1} = 3 \implies \gamma = 3\gamma - 3 \implies 2\gamma = 3 \implies \gamma = \frac{3}{2}$.

questions.question: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the $P\text{-}V$ diagram. Which curve represents the adiabatic process? (NEET 2022)
options: Curve with slope steeper than isothermal curve but with expansion
Horizontal line parallel to volume axis
Vertical line parallel to pressure axis
questions.solution: The slope of an adiabatic process on a $P\text{-}V$ indicator diagram is $\left(\frac{dP}{dV}\right)_{\text{ad}} = -\gamma \frac{P}{V}$, which is $\gamma$ times steeper than the slope of an isothermal process $\left(\frac{dP}{dV}\right)_{\text{iso}} = -\frac{P}{V}$.

questions.question: A sample of $0.1\text{ g}$ of water at $100^\circ\text{C}$ and normal atmospheric pressure ($1.013 \times 10^5\text{ N/m}^2$) requires $54\text{ cal}$ of heat energy to convert to steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$. If the volume of the steam produced is $167.1\text{ cc}$, the change in internal energy of the sample is: ($1\text{ cal} = 4.184\text{ J}$) (NEET 2018)
questions.solution:
Heat supplied $\Delta Q = 54 \times 4.184 = 225.94\text{ J}$.
Initial volume of liquid $V_1 = 0.1\text{ cc} = 0.1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$.
Final volume of steam $V_2 = 167.1\text{ cc} = 167.1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$.
$$\Delta W = P(V_2 - V_1) = 1.013 \times 10^5 \times (167.1 - 0.1) \times 10^{-6} = 1.013 \times 10^5 \times 167 \times 10^{-6} \approx 16.92\text{ J}$$
By First Law of Thermodynamics: $\Delta U = \Delta Q - \Delta W = 225.94 - 16.92 = 209.02\text{ J} \approx 208.7\text{ J}$.

questions.question: One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas undergoes a process described by the equation $P V^3 = \text{constant}$. The molar heat capacity of the gas during this process is: (NEET 2016)
questions.solution:
For a polytropic process $P V^x = \text{constant}$, molar heat capacity is $C = C_v + \frac{R}{1 - x}$.
For monoatomic gas, $C_v = \frac{3}{2}R$ and here $x = 3$.
$$C = \frac{3}{2}R + \frac{R}{1 - 3} = \frac{3}{2}R - \frac{R}{2} = R$$

questions.question: A Carnot engine having an efficiency of $\eta = 1/10$ as heat engine, is used as a refrigerator. If the work done on the system is $10\text{ J}$, the amount of energy absorbed from the cold reservoir at lower temperature is: (NEET 2017)
questions.solution:
Coefficient of performance $\beta = \frac{1 - \eta}{\eta} = \frac{1 - 0.1}{0.1} = 9$.
$$\beta = \frac{Q_2}{W} \implies Q_2 = \beta W = 9 \times 10\text{ J} = 90\text{ J}$$

questions.question: The efficiency of an ideal heat engine working between the freezing point and boiling point of water is: (NEET 2018)
Zeroth law of thermodynamics forms the fundamental basis for the measurement of:
questions.solution: The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics establishes that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other, defining temperature as a valid physical property.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a state function?
questions.solution: Work and heat are path-dependent functions, whereas internal energy, enthalpy, entropy, pressure, volume, and temperature depend solely on the thermodynamic state of the system.

questions.question: In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the work done by the gas is equal to:
questions.solution: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process ($T = \text{constant}$), internal energy change is zero ($\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T = 0$). By the First Law: $\Delta Q = \Delta U + W \implies W = \Delta Q$.

questions.question: An ideal gas expands isothermally from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$ and then is compressed adiabatically to its original volume $V_1$. If $W_1$ is the work done in the first process and $W_2$ is the work done in the second process, then:
questions.solution: The adiabatic curve on a $P\text{-}V$ diagram lies above the isothermal curve during compression ($P_{\text{adiabatic}} > P_{\text{isothermal}}$ for the same volume). Hence, the area under the adiabatic compression curve is greater, meaning $|W_2| > |W_1|$.

questions.question: During an adiabatic process, the equation relating temperature $T$ and volume $V$ for an ideal gas of ratio $\gamma$ is:
questions.solution: From $P V^\gamma = \text{constant}$ and ideal gas equation $P = \frac{nRT}{V}$, substituting $P$ gives $\left(\frac{T}{V}\right) V^\gamma = \text{constant} \implies T V^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$.

questions.question: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends ONLY upon its:
questions.solution: By Joule's law, there are no intermolecular attractive forces in an ideal gas, so its internal energy consists purely of kinetic energy and is solely a function of absolute temperature ($U = n C_v T$).

questions.question: Two moles of an ideal monoatomic gas ($\gamma = 5/3$) are compressed adiabatically from temperature $27^\circ\text{C}$ to $127^\circ\text{C}$. The work done on the gas during this process is: ($R = 8.31\text{ J/mol}\cdot\text{K}$)
questions.solution:
$$W = \frac{n R (T_1 - T_2)}{\gamma - 1} = \frac{2 \times 8.31 \times (300 - 400)}{5/3 - 1} = \frac{2 \times 8.31 \times (-100)}{2/3} = -3 \times 831 = -2493\text{ J}$$
Work done ON the gas is $|W| = 2493\text{ J}$.

questions.question: The Second Law of Thermodynamics rules out the existence of:
options: A $100\%$ efficient heat engine operating in a cycle
questions.solution: The Kelvin-Planck statement of the Second Law dictates that it is impossible to construct a cyclic heat engine whose sole effect is to absorb heat from a reservoir and convert it completely into mechanical work without rejecting any heat ($\eta < 100\%$ always).

questions.question: A thermodynamic system is taken through a cyclic process $ABCA$. If the net heat absorbed in the cycle is $+50\text{ J}$, the net work done by the system during the cycle is:
questions.solution:
For any complete cycle, the initial and final states are identical, so change in internal energy $\oint dU = 0$.
By the First Law: $W_{\text{net}} = Q_{\text{net}} = +50\text{ J}$.

questions.question: For an isobaric expansion of an ideal monoatomic gas, what fraction of the total heat supplied is converted into external work?
questions.solution:
For isobaric process: $\Delta Q = n C_p \Delta T$ and $\Delta W = n R \Delta T$.
$$\frac{\Delta W}{\Delta Q} = \frac{n R \Delta T}{n C_p \Delta T} = \frac{R}{C_p} = \frac{R}{\frac{5}{2}R} = \frac{2}{5}$$

questions.question: In an isochoric process, which of the following quantities is strictly ZERO?
questions.solution: In an isochoric process, volume is held constant ($dV = 0$), so the boundary work $W = \int P\,dV = 0$.

questions.question: An ideal gas undergoes an adiabatic compression. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Internal energy of the gas decreases
Heat is released to the surroundings
Work done on the gas is zero
questions.solution:
In an adiabatic compression, $\Delta Q = 0$ and work is done ON the gas ($W < 0$).
By First Law: $\Delta U = \Delta Q - W = 0 - (-|W|) = +|W| > 0$.
Since internal energy increases ($\,n C_v \Delta T > 0$), the temperature rises.

questions.question: The work done in an isothermal expansion of $n$ moles of an ideal gas from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$ at temperature $T$ is given by:
questions.solution: $$W = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} P\,dV = \int_{V_1}^{V_2} \frac{nRT}{V}\,dV = n R T \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$$

questions.question: A Carnot engine works between two temperatures $T_1 = 500\text{ K}$ and $T_2 = 300\text{ K}$. If it absorbs $600\text{ J}$ of heat from the source per cycle, the heat rejected to the sink per cycle is:
questions.solution:
For a reversible Carnot cycle: $\frac{Q_2}{Q_1} = \frac{T_2}{T_1}$.
$$Q_2 = Q_1 \left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right) = 600\text{ J} \times \left(\frac{300}{500}\right) = 360\text{ J}$$

questions.question: A gas is suddenly compressed to one-fourth of its original volume at constant temperature. If the initial pressure was $1\text{ atm}$, the final pressure will be:
questions.solution:
At constant temperature (isothermal process), $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$.
$$P_2 = P_1 \left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right) = 1\text{ atm} \times \left(\frac{V_1}{V_1/4}\right) = 4\text{ atm}$$

questions.question: Which of the following processes is IRREVERSIBLE in nature?
options: Free expansion of a gas into vacuum
questions.solution: Free expansion of a gas into an evacuated insulated container is an uncontrolled, non-equilibrium dissipative process and is completely irreversible.

questions.question: The slope of an isothermal curve and an adiabatic curve on a $P\text{-}V$ indicator diagram passing through the same $(P, V)$ point are related as:
questions.solution:
For isothermal: $\left(\frac{dP}{dV}\right)_T = -\frac{P}{V}$.
For adiabatic: $\left(\frac{dP}{dV}\right)_S = -\gamma \frac{P}{V} = \gamma \left(\frac{dP}{dV}\right)_T$.

questions.question: A system absorbs $300\text{ cal}$ of heat and at the same time does $400\text{ J}$ of work on the surroundings. The change in internal energy of the system is: ($1\text{ cal} = 4.184\text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
$\Delta Q = 300 \times 4.184 = 1255.2\text{ J}$.
Work done by system $W = +400\text{ J}$.
$$\Delta U = \Delta Q - W = 1255.2 - 400 = +855.2\text{ J}$$

questions.question: If an open door of a working household refrigerator is left open in a closed room, the room temperature will:
questions.solution: A refrigerator extracts heat $Q_2$ from its interior and rejects heat $Q_1 = Q_2 + W$ into the room. Since work $W$ performed by the compressor motor is dissipated as additional thermal energy, net heat is added to the room, increasing its temperature.

questions.question: During the free expansion of an ideal gas in an insulated container, which of the following remains constant?
questions.solution: For adiabatic free expansion into vacuum, $Q = 0$ and $W = 0$. By the First Law, $\Delta U = 0$. For an ideal gas ($U = f(T)$), $\Delta U = 0$ implies temperature $T$ remains constant.

questions.question: A monoatomic ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process represented by a circle on a $P\text{-}V$ diagram. If the coordinates of the center are $(P_0, V_0)$ and radii along $P$ and $V$ axes are $P_0/2$ and $V_0/2$, the net work done per cycle is:
questions.solution: Area of an ellipse/circle on $P\text{-}V$ diagram: $W = \pi a b = \pi \left(\frac{P_0}{2}\right) \left(\frac{V_0}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{4} P_0 V_0$.

questions.question: The molar heat capacity for an ideal gas in an isothermal process is:
questions.solution:
$$C = \frac{\Delta Q}{n \Delta T}$$
In an isothermal process, $\Delta T = 0$, so $C = \frac{\Delta Q}{0} = \infty$.

questions.question: The molar heat capacity of an ideal gas in an adiabatic process is:
questions.solution:
$$C = \frac{\Delta Q}{n \Delta T}$$
In an adiabatic process, $\Delta Q = 0$, so $C = \frac{0}{n \Delta T} = 0$.

questions.question: A diatomic gas ($\gamma = 1.4$) is compressed adiabatically to $\frac{1}{32}$ of its initial volume. If the initial temperature was $27^\circ\text{C}$, the final temperature is:
First law of thermodynamics is an expression of the universal law of:
questions.solution: The First Law of Thermodynamics ($\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$) is the statement of the principle of conservation of energy applied to thermodynamic systems.

questions.question: A Carnot engine operates with sink at $27^\circ\text{C}$ with an efficiency of $40\%$. By how much should the source temperature be increased to achieve an efficiency of $50\%$?
When an ideal gas undergoes an isobaric process from temperature $T_1$ to $T_2$, the work done by $n$ moles of gas is:
questions.solution: In an isobaric process: $W = P\Delta V = P(V_2 - V_1) = nR(T_2 - T_1)$.

questions.question: Clauseius statement of the Second Law of Thermodynamics deals with:
options: Transfer of heat from a colder body to a hotter body without external work
Conversion of heat completely into work
questions.solution: The Clausius statement asserts that it is impossible to construct a device operating in a cycle whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a cooler body to a hotter body without external work input.

questions.question: Equal volumes of monoatomic ($\gamma = 5/3$) and diatomic ($\gamma = 7/5$) gases at the same initial temperature and pressure are expanded adiabatically to double their volumes. The final pressure is:
questions.solution:
$P_f = P_i\left(\frac{V_i}{V_f}\right)^\gamma = P_i\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^\gamma$.
Since $\gamma_{\text{mono}} (1.67) > \gamma_{\text{dia}} (1.40)$, $(1/2)^{1.67} < (1/2)^{1.40}$. Therefore, $P_{f,\text{dia}} > P_{f,\text{mono}}$.

questions.question: A refrigerator works between $4^\circ\text{C}$ and $30^\circ\text{C}$. For every $1\text{ J}$ of mechanical energy supplied, the heat extracted from the interior is approximately:

An ideal gas is taken through a cycle $A \to B \to C \to A$ where $AB$ is isothermal expansion at $T$, $BC$ is isochoric cooling, and $CA$ is adiabatic compression. The net change in internal energy over one complete cycle is:
questions.solution: Internal energy is a thermodynamic state function. For any closed cycle returning to the starting state $A$, $\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = 0$ identically.

questions.question: For an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, which relationship is CORRECT?
questions.solution: Substituting $V = \frac{nRT}{P}$ into $PV^\gamma = \text{constant}$ yields $P\left(\frac{T}{P}\right)^\gamma = \text{constant} \implies P^{1-\gamma} T^\gamma = \text{constant}$.

questions.question: If $\Delta Q$ is added heat, $\Delta U$ is change in internal energy, and $\Delta W$ is work done, then for an isochoric process:
questions.solution: In an isochoric process, volume is fixed $\implies \Delta W = 0$. Hence, $\Delta Q = \Delta U$.

questions.question: During an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas at temperature $T$, the entropy change of the gas when its volume doubles is:
questions.solution: $$\Delta S = \int \frac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T} = \frac{W_{\text{iso}}}{T} = \frac{nRT \ln(V_2/V_1)}{T} = n R \ln(2)$$

questions.question: The total work done in the cyclic process shown in a $P\text{-}V$ loop is equal to:
options: Area under the expansion curve only
Area under the compression curve only
questions.solution: The net work done during a cyclic thermodynamic process is represented geometrically by the area enclosed by the closed curve on the $P\text{-}V$ indicator diagram (positive if clockwise, negative if counter-clockwise).

questions.question: A heat engine rejects $600\text{ J}$ of heat to the sink for every $1000\text{ J}$ of heat absorbed from the source. The efficiency of the engine is:
For a polytropic process $P V^n = \text{constant}$, the work done when an ideal gas goes from $(P_1, V_1, T_1)$ to $(P_2, V_2, T_2)$ is:
Which of the following conditions ensures that a thermodynamic process is REVERSIBLE?
options: The process must be quasi-static and completely free of dissipative forces
The process must be extremely rapid
There must be large temperature differences across boundaries
questions.solution: A reversible process requires the system to pass infinitely slowly through a continuous sequence of equilibrium states (quasi-static) without any dissipative effects such as friction, viscosity, or inelasticity.

questions.question: When $2\text{ moles}$ of an ideal gas are heated at constant pressure from $300\text{ K}$ to $400\text{ K}$, the work done by the gas is: ($R = 8.31\text{ J/mol}\cdot\text{K}$)
questions.solution: $$W = P\Delta V = n R\Delta T = 2 \times 8.31 \times (400 - 300) = 2 \times 8.31 \times 100 = 1662\text{ J}$$
